article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_title: Which Highway Really Has The Highest Number Of Lanes?
title: Which Highway Really Has The Highest Number Of Lanes?
raw_summary: Freeways are to people what arteries are to red blood cells. Most freeways consist of three or four lanes of synchronized traffic flow (or collective halt), but have you ever wondered what the world record is for the highest number of lanes on a freeway? The obvious choice would be the Katy Freeway on I-10 just west of Houston, which has no fewer than 26 traffic lanes spread across both directions at its widest. However, that number also includes feeder roads that don't actually form part of the I-10, so it's often argued that the "true" number is actually 18. If that's the case, a few other massive highways may indeed lay claim to Katy's title as the highest-lane highway in the world. Canada, for instance, has an 18-lane road approaching one of its airports, while Burma's capital city has a section with up to 20 lanes. However, perhaps the biggest threats sit halfway across the globe in China. These include a special section of the G4 Beijing–Hong Kong-Macau Expressway and the Hefei–Nanjing Expressway, the latter of which can open up to as many as 36 separate lanes — but with one very important caveat. Let's take a look at some of the highest-lane freeways in the world and how they compare before crowning the winner.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Jalopnik, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

title: High altitude, bitter cold, zero drivers: autonomous trucks take on Tibetan mine
raw_summary: Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks . Chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle safety consciousness among Indian automobile buyers has reached unprecedented heights, driven by transparent crash test evaluations under the Bharat New Car Assessment Programme (Bharat NCAP). Verified technical telemetry reported by Electrek provides a detailed examination of structural crashworthiness and passenger protection ratings for Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Under Bharat NCAP protocols, vehicles undergo rigorous offset frontal crash tests at 64 kmph, side mobile deformable barrier impacts at 50 kmph, and stringent pole side-impact evaluations. To secure a coveted 5-star safety rating, a vehicle must achieve high numerical scores in Adult Occupant Protection (AOP) and Child Occupant Protection (COP), while critically demonstrating that the passenger bodyshell remains 'Stable and capable of withstanding further loadings'.

What separates truly crash-resilient vehicles from mere marketing claims is the extensive deployment of advanced high-strength steel (AHSS) and ultra-high-strength hot-stamped steel along the A-pillars, B-pillars, and door sills. Standard fitment of 6 airbags, Electronic Stability Control (ESC), ISOFIX child seat anchorages, and 3-point seatbelts with pre-tensioners across all seating positions has now become the fundamental benchmark for modern Indian buyers.

In real-world highway collisions, vehicles with unstable cabin architectures risk severe footwell intrusion, steering column collapse, and door jamming that traps occupants inside. Indian carmakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra have raised the bar by engineering 5-star crash resilience into their entry and mid-size platforms, compelling global competitors to rapidly upgrade their structural standards.

Our consumer verdict: never compromise on core structural integrity for cosmetic add-ons like ambient lighting or fancy touchscreens. Prioritize vehicles with certified 5-star Bharat NCAP or Global NCAP ratings, verified stable bodyshell integrity, and standard Electronic Stability Program (ESP) to ensure maximum survivability on unpredictable Indian roads.

We've seen the warnings from informational videos over the decades , and our personal blunders and experiences have demonstrated this point, too . We can, of course, be attentive behind the wheel, but that doesn't account for the others who aren't while on the road. It's partly why dash cams and their resulting videos have gained so much traction in recent years. While someone's dumb decision may end up in disaster, others might end in close calls — moments where destruction was inches away. Close calls happen more often than you might expect, especially when we live in an era where vehicles are equipped with every warning along with literal bells and whistles to tell drivers they might hit something. This week, we don't want to know about the little near-misses — we want to know about the big ones that haunt you. Tell us about the misses that had they been hits, would've made for calamity.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Instead of being a Miata fighter, the new S-FR would be even smaller, built on the platform of a third-generation Daihatsu Copen . Daihatsu teased a new Copen with its K-Open concept last year (pictured below), and it wouldn't be hard for Toyota to throw a bit of design work at its subsidiary's kei car and bring a proper S-FR to market.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Jalopnik, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: 12 Plug-In Hybrids With The Longest Electric-Only Range
raw_summary: Back in 2010, Chevrolet introduced the groundbreaking Volt — America's first plug-in hybrid production car. Packing a fairly big 16-kWh battery pack, the Volt had an EPA-estimated electric range of 35 miles, with later first-generation models rated at up to 38 miles. When the battery was depleted, it turned to a 1.4-liter four-cylinder engine with 84 horsepower to cover longer distances. Although it ultimately failed to attract enough buyers and was discontinued in 2019, the Chevrolet Volt was so far ahead of its time that many current PHEVs struggle to match its electric range. In fact, out of the 12 plug-in hybrids with the longest electric-only range on sale right now, four have lower range figures. Of course, many modern PHEVs offer more EV range, with some models, like the 2027 Land Rover Range Rover Plug-in Hybrid, 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC 350e 4MATIC, and 2027 Toyota RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid, capable of delivering 50 miles of driving without calling on the internal combustion engine.

raw_title: 5 Generations Of The Chevy Impala SS Ranked From Best To Worst Horsepower Ratings
title: 5 Generations Of The Chevy Impala SS Ranked From Best To Worst Horsepower Ratings
raw_summary: Mention a Chevy Impala, and thoughts of an unremarkable family sedan may come to mind, but add an SS next to the nameplate and things change. The Impala SS (Super Sport) is a pure horsepower play that dates back to 1961, two years after the Bowtie brand launched the Impala as a standalone model. Its numbers are still impressive, even by 21st-century standards. The retail version of the Impala SS from the 1960s, which covered two generations, produced up to 425 horsepower. The later Impala SS generations from the 1990s and 2000s were less brutish, offering between 240 and 303 hp, but they were still a step up from their more mundane counterparts. However, these horsepower numbers come with a catch. The output figures for 1960s Impala SS models reflected gross horsepower ratings, which generally didn't account for intake, exhaust, and accessory loads. When the 1970s rolled around, the auto industry was dealing with tighter emissions regulations and insurance companies that took a dim view of high-powered cars. By the 1972 model year, Detroit switched to net horsepower calculations to better reflect real-world engine configurations. Because gross horsepower ratings often varied from manufacturer to manufacturer, there's no standard way to convert horsepower ratings between the methods, but both still measure horsepower at the crankshaft, not the wheels.

raw_title: Can Directional Tires Be Rotated From One Side To The Other?
title: Can Directional Tires Be Rotated From One Side To The Other?
raw_summary: Technically, directional tires can be rotated from one side of a car to the other. Nobody can stop you from unbolting a wheel/tire combo from one side of the car and putting it on the other side. The catch is that doing it properly involves more work than unbolting the wheels and swapping their positions. Skip that extra work and those carefully designed tread patterns will end up running backward. That might not sound all that terrible, but for these "unidirectional" tires, the rolling direction matters. Crossing directional tires requires removing them from their wheels and remounting them in the correct orientation for the opposite side. Each one then needs rebalancing, which is where the red and yellow dots on tires come in. So sure, you can unbolt whatever is on the passenger side of your car and swap it to the driver's side. But the tread will be heading in the wrong direction. Still, there are other ways to do this job without messing anything up.

As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: Mini Truck Vs. Side-By-Side: What Are The Practical Differences?
raw_summary: You've likely seen those neat little mini trucks from Japan. They're the size of a compact vehicle, but have a bed as long as some full-size pickups. These Kei trucks, as they are called, look like they would be pretty practical for a number of uses. President Trump was quite smitten with Kei trucks when he saw them in Japan, apparently for the first time, later calling them "really cute." And in a December 2025 Truth Social post, he said that he had "approved" the manufacture of these "tiny" vehicles here. But, as is the case with many of the president's statements, no one is quite sure what that means. Unfortunately, you can't buy a new one for road use in the U.S., but older ones are available thanks to an exception in import laws.
